1.point: The prayers first ask for the heart to be severed from everything but God; what goes is the heart's love of the world, not the world, so nobody is asked to leave family or society.
steps: The Munajat's request for light follows a request to be cut off, so severance is the first request.
The word inqitaʿ could be read as a call to abandon family, work and society.
Abu Hamza names what is cut: love of the world from the heart, not the world itself.
The friends of God keep their families and place in society, so the severance is in the heart.

2.point: Once free, the heart is asked to see God, love Him and draw near Him, and these are the knowing and love Chapter One set as ʿirfan's two aims.
steps: A freed heart is free for God; the prayers then ask three things.
Sight: the Munajat asks for the eye of the heart to be lit; the Qur'an's 'sight cannot perceive Him' is met by distinguishing physical eyes from the heart's eye.
Love: the Munajat asks for a place among God's friends, defined by love; the Sheikh reads wilaya as maʿrifah plus love, the two aims of ʿirfan.
Nearness: the Munajat asks to be brought near.

3.point: The prayers speak from need and humility in words far above us (a pupil with a university book); the answer is that we are honoured to be allowed to say them and a sincere reciter may be granted the request.
steps: The difficulty: these words belong to the muqarrabun, so why are ordinary believers told to recite them?
The prayers themselves speak from need, as a pupil would.
They go further in humility: even the turning to God is His doing.
The answer rests on that humility: not understanding does not make them meaningless; we are honoured, and God may grant the request.

4.point: These are Mafatih prayers set on nights believers already keep; few reach their depth (Maliki Tabrizi) but anyone may begin (the Sheikh); the chapter claims access, not attainment.
steps: Four of the prayers are in the Mafatih, each set on a night or day.
The Munajat belongs to Shaʿban; the others have their own nights.
Those nights make the words familiar.
Familiarity is not attainment: Maliki Tabrizi says few comprehend them.
The Sheikh still recommends them to everyone; the two answer different questions; the claim is access.

5.point: The goal of ʿirfan is already on the believer's lips: the prayers kept on ordinary nights ask, from need, for severance, sight, love and nearness.
steps: Access to these words is where the ordinary believer already stands.
The prayers ask for the knowing and love that ʿirfan aims at, in the voice of need, on ordinary nights.
So the goal of ʿirfan is not foreign; it is already on our lips.

¶1.label: advance
¶1.why: Establishes that the request for light follows a request to be cut off: severance is the first request.

¶2.label: advance
¶2.why: Names inqitaʿ and raises the misreading (leave family, work, society) that the section exists to rule out.

¶3.label: advance
¶3.why: Abu Hamza supplies what is cut: love of the world from the heart, not the world. This is the point's core distinction.

¶4.label: support
¶4.why: The friends of God keeping their families is evidence for ¶3's step and carries the 'not withdrawal from society' half of the point; the closing sentence repeats ¶3.

¶5.label: aside
¶5.why: That God has already done the severance for those He loves is a new idea the point does not need; nothing later depends on it.

¶6.label: aside
¶6.why: Gloss on the ¶5 quotation ('God's own work', 'nothing but love'); neither idea is used by the point or by Section 2.

¶7.label: advance
¶7.why: Links the freed heart to the three requests and announces them.

¶8.label: advance
¶8.why: First request, sight, with the Qur'anic difficulty that ¶9 must resolve.

¶9.label: advance
¶9.why: Resolves the difficulty: physical eyes cannot, the heart's eye can; this is what the prayer asks to have lit.

¶10.label: aside
¶10.why: A second prayer saying God has already lit the friends' hearts; the point needs only that the prayers ask for sight, which ¶8-9 gave.

¶11.label: aside
¶11.why: Cross-references to Chapter One and Two and the claim 'the lighting of any heart is God's act' are not used by this section's point or any later paragraph.

¶12.label: advance
¶12.why: Second request, love: a place among God's friends defined by love.

¶13.label: advance
¶13.why: Wilaya read as maʿrifah plus love and identified with Chapter One's two aims of ʿirfan, the point's final clause.

¶14.label: advance
¶14.why: Third request, nearness, with its Munajat line.

¶15.label: aside
¶15.why: A second prayer asking for the same nearness ('love the meeting'); ¶14 already supplied the step and nothing later uses this.

¶16.label: aside
¶16.why: A third prayer on nearness; adds another source, not a step.

¶17.label: aside
¶17.why: Reflection on how calling on God feels for 'some of us' and 'others'; the point does not need it and no later sentence picks it up.

¶18.label: advance
¶18.why: States the difficulty: words of the muqarrabun given to a primary school pupil.

¶19.label: advance
¶19.why: The prayers speak from need; ʿArafah supplies the first instance.

¶20.label: aside
¶20.why: 'makes the same plea': a second prayer repeating ¶19's step; the door image is not used later.

¶21.label: advance
¶21.why: Moves from need to humility (even the turning to God is His doing), which ¶22 explicitly rests on.

¶22.label: advance
¶22.why: Gives the answer: not understanding is not meaninglessness; we are honoured; God may grant a sincere reciter's request.

¶23.label: advance
¶23.why: The prayers are in the Mafatih and set on nights and days: the section's first step.

¶24.label: support
¶24.why: The Munajat's place in Shaʿban is the instance ¶26 ('these nights') and ¶28 ('recited in Shaʿban') use.

¶25.label: support
¶25.why: The other prayers' nights give the plural 'nights believers already keep' that ¶26 relies on.

¶26.label: advance
¶26.why: Draws the step 'the words are familiar', which ¶27 turns on; the Khomeini quotation is the evidence.

¶27.label: advance
¶27.why: Familiarity is not attainment: Maliki Tabrizi says few comprehend them.

¶28.label: advance
¶28.why: The Sheikh's recommendation, the reconciliation of the two, and the chapter's claim of access not attainment.

¶29.label: restate
¶29.why: Summarises Part One, Chapter Two and the four requests already established in Sections 1-2; only the first sentence ('where an ordinary believer already stands') is new and ¶30 could carry it.

¶30.label: advance
¶30.why: States the conclusion for the first time: the goal of ʿirfan is already on our lips (the Appendix note is housekeeping).

¶31.label: aside
¶31.why: A question raised and not answered here ('What is this self?'); the section's point does not need it.
